summary: Discovery call to understand Catalina Systems' model selection needs for a multilingual, tool-calling product. Customer leaning toward Hosted for fast evaluation, Dedicated or Private for production due to compliance. Key concerns: context length (32k vs 8k), tool/function calling reliability, latency vs cost trade-offs, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: pricing, POC scheduling, and sharing sample data.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-10-11 08:43 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Catalina VP Eng), Evan Chu (Catalina ML Infra), Rana Sethi (Catalina Security), Tom Briggs (Catalina Product)

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 40 minutes, appreciate you all making time. quick intros?
[00:08] Marta: Hi I'm Marta, VP engineering at Catalina, we build a customer support augmentation product that needs long context and multi language.
[00:14] Evan: Evan, ML infra, i'll be driving the POC and benchmarks.
[00:18] Rana: Rana, security and compliance.
[00:20] Tom: Tom, product, mostly roadmap and success criteria.
[00:24] Jared: Great. Priya, want to say hi?
[00:25] Priya: Yep, hi all, SE on Redwood, i'll do the tech deep dive and we'll talk model options and deployment modes.
[00:30] Jared: Quick agenda: understanding your current stack, pain, then model selection constraints — context length, multilingual, tool calling, then deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), and next steps.
[00:40] Marta: That sounds good. Broadly, our app ingests multi-day chat logs, we need 20k–32k tokens of context for full convo summarization and routing. Latency target is under 1s per assistant response for interactive flows, but batch summarization can tolerate 3–5s. Cost is a big factor, especially at scale.
[01:05] Priya: ok good, so 32k upper bound is useful. We typically map 8k vs 32k support to different model families and quantization. Are you expecting realtime qps?
[01:14] Evan: Peak qps is 80 during business hours, avg 20, concurrency up to 12. We'll run a baseline of sample traffic.
[01:22] Tom: Also want reliable tool/function calling — we call internal APIs for ticket creation and agent lookups, so deterministic function call behavior matters.
[01:30] Rana: And from security we need data residency, KMS encryption, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence. If possible VPC/private deployment would be preferable for production.
[01:40] Jared: Great, lets talk models. For 32k context we recommend a few open families — Llama 3 variants, Mistral longformer-ish forks, and some of the community 1.6/1.8 models. Priya, can you describe performance tradeoffs?
[01:52] Priya: Sure. Short version: 8k context models are much cheaper and faster. 32k models need more memory, so throughput drops and per-token cost increases. We have two main paths: Hosted with Redwood-managed long-context models (we run compressed KV caching and prefix cache to reduce tokens), or Dedicated where you can pin a quantized 32k model on reserved GPU with predictable throughput. Private is similar to Dedicated but with customer-managed VPC and KMS for compliance.
[02:25] Marta: Any differences in function-calling reliability between Hosted and Dedicated? we saw inconsistent fn-calls in a quick open-source test.
[02:33] Priya: Function-calling is primarily model behavior + runtime handling. Hosted includes our function-calling orchestration and fallback policies — e.g., if model returns ambiguous tool intent, we can route to a smaller deterministic reranker or run a second pass. On Dedicated we can configure the same runtime features, but you'd need the policy configs — we provide them. The big difference is SLA and isolation.
[02:58] Evan: For POC we'd like to run the same prompts against 8k and 32k variants, measure latencies and token costs. Also test tool calling with simultaneous requests.
[03:08] Priya: totally — we can spin up a POC environment on Hosted to validate function-calling and 32k model behavior. If you want private network, Dedicated private VPC can be arranged for later.
[03:18] Rana: Are there any requirements for keys and encryption on Hosted? we need KMS integration and key control.
[03:24] Jared: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for enterprise customers; we also have an option to encrypt at rest and provide audit logs. For strict key control and air-gapped needs, Private/on-prem is the option.
[03:36] Tom: On multilingual — we need good support across Spanish, Portuguese, French, and some East Asian languages. Latency should not degrade much when using multilingual models.
[03:46] Priya: Many open models are multilingual but quality varies. We typically recommend fine-tuning or prompt-engineering + a small reranker to ensure parity. For top quality across languages, we can test a multilingual Llama-family and a Mistral-ish variant; also we can run evals on your sample prompts.
[04:05] Marta: Does Redwood provide eval tooling? we have datasets already.
[04:08] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize provides evaluation harnesses — you can upload evaluation prompts, and we'll run A/B tests across candidate models and metrics like hallucination rate, function-calling accuracy, latency and per-token cost.
[04:20] Evan: A few nitty gritty infra questions: do you support continuous batching and KV cache? how about returning cached prefixes to save tokens?
[04:29] Priya: We do continuous batching in the runtime and KV cache for decoder-only models; we also support prefix caching which can reduce per-request cost significantly for repeated conversational context. There are tradeoffs with latency, but we can tune batch windows.
[04:45] Marta: For the POC, can we run 32k and test memory footprint on a single GPU? we use A100s in-house.
[04:52] Priya: Yes, we can test on A100s. Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools and we can recommend quantization profiles that let a 32k model run within memory, with some performance tradeoffs. For pure fidelity you'd run fp16 on larger GPUs.
[05:06] Tom: What about streaming and partial responses? our UX expects first token within 200–300ms ideally.
[05:12] Priya: Streaming first token times depend on model size and whether you're serving with small batch windows. For 8k models it's achievable sub-300ms with tuned kernels; for 32k it's harder but we can still hit interactive ranges by prioritizing low-latency routing and smaller batch thresholds. There's a cost tradeoff.
[05:30] Evan: Speaking of cost, do you have a unit economics calc? we need to compare Hosted per-token vs Dedicated amortized GPU cost.
[05:37] Jared: We'll send a calc — sample numbers for 8k vs 32k, with batching and caching assumptions. Dedicated has upfront commit but predictable monthly unit cost; Hosted is elastic and easier to pilot.
[05:48] Rana: Compliance again — do you log transcripts? how long are logs retained and can we configure retention for audit?
[05:55] Jared: Yes we capture audit logs and can configure retention per contract. For Hosted we keep logs per your policy and can push logs into your S3 via secure transfer. For Private, log control is entirely yours.
[06:07] Marta: Any known model gotchas for tool-calling? we had problems where the model would hallucinate a function name and not follow schema.
[06:14] Priya: That's common. We mitigate with structured function schemas, rerankers, and deterministic post-processing. Also sometimes the model needs prompt scaffolding to pick the right tool. We'll include examples.
[06:28] Tom: For the POC we'd like 3 candidate models: one cost-optimized 8k, one 32k long-context, and a multilingual model. Can Redwood help shortlist?
[06:36] Priya: Yes, we'll propose 3 — likely a quantized Llama variant for cost, a longform Llama/Mistral variant for 32k, and a multilingual family. We'll run your evals.
[06:46] Marta: About rollout strategy — dream state is canary on Dedicated then full roll to Dedicated or Private.
[06:52] Jared: That's a standard path. Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B, and auto-fallback policies to smaller models when degraded.
[06:59] Evan: For the tech POC, what telemetry do we get? token-level cost, latency histograms, per-route dashboards?
[07:06] Priya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. We'll demo that if you want.
[07:16] Rana: On SSO and RBAC — we need SAML and SCIM and fine-grained roles.
[07:21] Jared: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC controls in the enterprise package.
[07:27] Tom: For benchmarks, can we run synthetic load similar to our concurrency pattern?
[07:31] Priya: Absolutely — provide the qps and concurrency and we'll replicate. We'll also test P50/P95 latency.
[07:38] Marta: Any limits on model customizations or fine-tuning for Hosted?
[07:42] Priya: On Hosted we support prompt-tuning and lightweight fine-tuning for select models; Dedicated and Private give more latitude for customer-managed fine-tune artifacts. We'll clarify model-specific constraints.
[07:53] Evan: Ok, let's talk timing: we'd like to start POC next week if possible and aim for production decision in 6–8 weeks.
[08:00] Jared: That timeline is reasonable. We'll push pricing and schedule the POC quickstart.
[08:04] Marta: One more — latency target under 1s for interactive is strict, would you recommend hybrid approach?
[08:10] Priya: Yes, hybrid is common: interactive routes to an 8k model with context window narrowed to the last N tokens, while background summarization runs on 32k for full context. That reduces latency and cost while preserving long-context fidelity.
[08:24] Tom: That sounds like a good pattern.
[08:26] Rana: Security question — how do you handle KMS rotation and side-loaded keys?
[08:31] Jared: We support customer-managed KMS with rotation policies; for Private/on-prem we can work with HSM integrations. We'll share the security pack.
[08:39] Marta: ok great, can we recap next steps?
[08:41] Jared: Sure — i'll send the cost calc and Hosted vs Dedicated comparison; Priya will schedule the POC and shortlist models; Evan will send sample prompts and traffic; Rana will request SOC2/compliance items. We'll target initial POC run next week.
[08:53] Tom: thanks all.
[08:55] Jared: Thanks, wrap up.
[09:00] [call end]
